doc: Background props that look like lights but have no baked E: census kind 'prop', bake class 'glow' (their own tile slots; one per character in the actor lights). Candidates from `sandover-lights inventory` (kb/findings/2026-09-27-light-inventory.md). A prop gives light only where the game draws it brighter than its surroundings: `vanilla` holds `sandover-lights glowcheck` on vanilla rig frames (frame names under the $SANDOVER_DATA capture sets, provenance only; contrast = median luma over the surroundings' within 5 m, ceiling = share of its / their pixels at 250+), saturation = (max - min) / max of its mean colour; the bake applies props.glows_in_vanilla (contrast >= 1.3 and saturation >= 0.6, or ceiling >= 0.5 and twice the surroundings'; a texture with non-zero baked E on the level (a census static: the game treats it as an emitter, at some hour) needs only the contrast, and its statics are dropped before the caps). No frame: no light. Colour: texture x vertex colour (`colour_from: texture` = texture alone). Patches are clustered on `cell_m` grids: a patch is one light, so its one shadow map shadows all of its light.

snow-crystals.note: pale blue ice crystal clusters (snow-vis-shrub); no baked E; drawn at the SDR ceiling in vanilla (93-96% of their pixels, `vanilla`); a soft cool light and a very weak shadow (runs/20260926-1011-play 0019); colour from the texture alone: the level's blue vertex tint is its ambient, not the crystal's

cv-bluecrystal.note: pale blue crystal clusters on the cave walls; drawn at the SDR ceiling in vanilla (97-99% of their pixels, `vanilla`); colour from the texture alone: the caves' teal vertex tint is their ambient (crystals-004 read green-cyan, R 0)

ogr-cave-crystal-01.note: red-pink crystal clusters along the Mountain Pass (ogre tie); census statics too, but their baked E sits on the night source only, so the static rows lit them only at night; drawn 3x brighter than the rock around them at noon in vanilla (pale: saturation 0.32-0.42; the emitter branch of glows_in_vanilla applies because the level bakes E for the texture); colour from the texture alone

cv-mushroom-01-decal-01.note: glowing green cave mushrooms (bright green in 0021); green from the vertex colours

cv-tallshroom-decal-01.note: tall glowing green cave mushrooms, as cv-mushroom-01-decal-01

ogr-mushroom-whole-01.note: teal-capped mushrooms; drawn brighter than 99% of the level

ya-mushroom-whole-01.note: teal-capped mushrooms (same art as ogre's); brighter than 93% of the level

vil3-mushroom-01.note: pale blue cave mushrooms; brighter than 80% of the level; kept on a 1 m grid: village3's mushrooms stand apart, and a 12 m patch put the light 6-7 m from them

vil3-mushroom-02.note: pale blue cave mushrooms; brighter than 88% of the level; kept on a 1 m grid: village3's mushrooms stand apart, and a 12 m patch put the light 6-7 m from them

vil3-giant-crystal-nt-01.note: teal giant crystals without baked E (their vil3-crystal-01 neighbours are statics already)

vil3-giant-crystal-nt-03.note: pale translucent giant crystals, as vil3-giant-crystal-nt-01

jngb-precursor-circuitpattern-andwall-02.note: precursor glow circuitry (white glow overlay); brighter than 87% of the level

jngb-precursor-spheres-glow.note: precursor glow spikes on the spheres; brighter than 93% of the level

cit-pinkbeam.note: pink light beams; brighter than 98% of the level; long, so 12 m tiles at half gain

lava-vent-fire.note: fire in the lava vents; brighter than 99% of the level

lava-precursor-bluelight.note: blue precursor lights; brighter than 99.9% of the level
